access_notes: Read by eye at full size and at 3x on the face. The file carries no capture or software metadata (EXIF: orientation and 72 dpi only), so where and when the picture was made cannot be read from it. asset_use is cross_check, not geometry: a tier-5 picture is not evidence of anyone's outline (docs/PROVENANCE.md). The model's face is fitted to it only because the owner chose it as the stand-in likeness; that face is a liberty graded reconstructed (docs/LIBERTIES.md, L-prairie-likenesses-3547), not a measurement of the person.
note: THIS IS NOT A PHOTOGRAPH OF WILLIAM L. GREY. No photograph of William L. Grey has been found (the household record's portrait search, docs/RESEARCH/prairie-portraits-3546). The owner chose this picture as the stand-in for William L. Grey's face, hair and dress, as the Glessner household's stand-ins were chosen (T-3478). A sepia cabinet-style portrait, three-quarter length: a broad-faced, freckled man of middle age seated in a carved armchair before a painted studio backdrop (foliage at left, a column at right), his wavy hair worn long over the ears and swept back from a high forehead, a full trimmed beard and moustache, in a dark three-piece suit, a white standing collar and a dark patterned four-in-hand tie, a watch chain looped across the waistcoat. His face is turned a little to his left and lit from the left, both eyes and his right ear showing; about 120 px between the pupils.
